items.caption:
Please don’t skip your skin checks. 💛

Nearly three years ago, I was diagnosed with melanoma, and today was another one of my regular skin check appointments.

I still get anxious before every visit because you never know what they might find, but I’d rather have that worry than ignore something that could be serious.

Thankfully, today’s check was all clear. They did freeze one mole that had been rubbing on my clothes, but everything else looked good.

If my journey has taught me anything, it’s this: wear your SPF, get to know your skin, and never ignore a changing mole. Early detection really can save lives.

Have you checked your skin recently? 💛☀️

#melanomaawareness #skincancer
items.transcript: Nearly three years ago I was diagnosed with invasive melanoma and ever since then I've had regular skin checks. I still get so nervous before every appointment because you never know what they might find. Melanoma doesn't just go away, which is why ongoing checks are essential. If you notice a new mole or change to an existing one, please get it checked. And don't forget to wear your SPF every single day. Looking after your skin and catching changes early really can save your life. Thankfully today's check was all clear and I'm so grateful.

items.caption:
Cleaning Myths BUSTED! 🤯

This time I skipped the supermarket and busted some of the biggest cleaning myths right here at home!

Did any of these surprise you? 

Maybe the one about hot water… or perhaps vacuuming? 👀

Watch the video and let me know

Thanks for watching 💖

#cleaningmyths #queenofclean
items.transcript: You know how we've been doing these cleaning myth videos out and about? Well, I thought today we'd buff some cleaning myths at home. Myth number one, dishwashers. Because you're actually using it to clean your plates or putting a product in it, does it actually need cleaning? Well, the answer is yes, of course it does. If you don't clean your dishwasher, empty out the filter. It's not going to clean your dishes properly. Myth number two, do you need to deep clean your house more than once a week? The answer to that one is no, you don't. Once a week for a deep clean is absolutely perfect if you're doing those small maintenance cleans in between. And if you've got my book, The 15 Minute Clean, this will teach you how to clean your house in just 15 minutes. Number three, you should always clean your glass on your windows on a sunny day. Well, that is completely wrong. You want to clean your windows on the dullest, miserable day possible, but preferably when it's not raining like it is today. Reason being, as soon as product hits the glass, it's going to dry, it's going to cause those streaks, and that is caused by the sun. So stick to those dull days and a good lint-free window cleaning cloth. Myth number four, hot water is needed for all household cleaning. The answer to that one is no, you don't need to use boiling hot water or even really hot water from the tap. Reasons being is hot water can cause more streaks when you're cleaning glass and glass surfaces. It can also damage wooden surfaces if you've got wooden worktops, and it can also evaporate some cleaning products. The last myth today is myth number five, does vacuuming your carpets every single day damage them? The answer to that one is no, but please always make sure that your vacuum is set on the correct floor type. If you're vacuuming carpets, make sure it's set to carpet, and if you're doing hard floors, make sure it's set to hard floors. So that was five more myths busted, and this time we were at home. Come back for more soon.

Ice Cube Hack ✨

Got creased clothes but no time to get the iron out? Simply pop your garment into the tumble dryer with some ice cubes and run it on a high heat for around 10 minutes. As the ice melts, it creates steam that helps relax the fabric and reduce creases, leaving many items ready to wear in minutes.

💡 Best for lightweight fabrics and small loads.

Stop fruit flies fast with this simple summer hack!

Fill a recycled jar with a splash of white vinegar and a few drops of washing-up liquid, then make a few small holes in the lid.

The vinegar attracts the fruit flies, while the washing-up liquid breaks the surface tension so they become trapped.

Place it near your fruit bowl or food waste bin for the best results. Simple, inexpensive and surprisingly effective!

Have you tried this hack? 👇
